speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, have you noticed if your joint pain worsens during periods of inactivity or if it improves with movement? Also, how would you describe the sensation, such as stiffness, swelling, or warmth?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gouty Arthritis with secondary degenerative joint disease (osteoarthritis). The clinical picture of 69-year-old male with progressive worsening pain in the left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest is consistent with gout and osteoarthritis. REQUEST IMAGES: Left foot X-ray, Hip X-ray, Knee X-ray.
